newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi wants speedy end to Saudi airlines debt.
newsitem.headline: Saudi wants speedy end to Saudi airlines debt.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's defence and aviation minister has ordered a speedy resolution to outstanding payments owed by Saudi Arabian Airlines Corp to Riyad Bank, Saudi newspapers said on Monday.

They said the bank had released a statement saying Prince Sultan had issued an order "to find the appropriate solutions in the near future for these debts", and the formation of a special committee to deal with the issue.
Riyad Bank, Saudi Arabia's second biggest, has been in talks with the state-owned airlines to clear outstanding payments on the three billion riyal ($800 million) loan.
A statement from the bank acknowledged for the first time publicly that it had delayed publishing 1996 third quarter results due to fruitless efforts to settle a debt problem with a client.
It did not name the client.
Officials at Riyad Bank, the most heavily traded blue chip on the Saudi stock market last year, were not available for comment.
A Saudi trader on Monday said news of developments in the debt talks appeared to have no direct impact on market confidence in the bank.
Saudi legislation demands public shareholding firms to publish third quarter results in the fourth quarter. ($1=3.75 riyals)
